## 1. Boot the app

Start the server from the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY:

It listens on http://localhost:4173. If port 4173 is already in use, something is wrong

## 2. Drive the browser, in this order

1. Start a Playwright trace now, before navigating anywhere. Use raw code
   execution ONLY to start and stop the trace; drive everything else with
   the ordinary browser tools. This has to come first: a trace only captures
   the network resources (CSS, fonts, images) requested while it is
   running. If the page navigates before the trace starts, its stylesheet
   is never captured — every snapshot you take later will still reference

2. Navigate to the page the work item describes (or the closest match under

3. Set a desktop viewport immediately.
4. Get the app into whatever starting state the work item's repro steps

5. Snapshot the initial state.
6. Perform the exact sequence of actions the work item describes as
   triggering the failure, in the order it describes them. Snapshot after
   any step the work item calls out as significant (e.g. one that should
   succeed before the one that fails).
7. WAIT after the final triggering action, at least a few seconds, before
   concluding nothing happened. If the report mentions users clicking again,
   the page "not responding," or anything else suggesting the failure isn't

   trace right after the action is the single most common way to lose this
   kind of evidence. Snapshot again after waiting.
8. Collect console messages and network requests (status codes and response
   bodies) for whatever request(s) the work item implicates.
9. While the failure state is still on screen and the trace is STILL
   RUNNING, take an explicit full-page screenshot with the browser's
   screenshot tool (not the accessibility snapshot from steps 5/6/7 — an
   actual image) and save it into /workspaces/01a007f4-6dd4-732f-9e9d-f8459d275e84/.scarn/step-artifacts/. Do this
   regardless of what the failure actually turned out to be (banner, popup,
   redirected page, etc.) — whatever is on screen when you take it is what
   gets baked in.

   This step exists because the Playwright trace viewer only ever shows a
   small live-view thumbnail of whatever the page looked like when the
   trace was stopped; that thumbnail is easy to miss and isn't a real frame

   the trace is recording becomes a real, inspectable action in the trace
